explanation: After the Mexican Revolution, the government paid him to paint history on public walls. In New York, his 1933 Rockefeller Center mural was destroyed because it showed Lenin.

claims.text: Diego Rivera is famous chiefly for large public murals.
Rivera is not known for marble sculpture, woodblock prints or stained-glass windows.
After the Mexican Revolution, the Mexican government commissioned Rivera and other artists to paint murals on public buildings.
Rivera's 1933 mural at the Rockefeller Center in New York was destroyed after he refused to remove a portrait of Lenin from it.

evidence.restatement: Rivera is best known for large public murals.
He is not known for marble sculpture, woodblock prints or stained glass.
From the early 1920s the post-revolutionary government, under education minister José Vasconcelos, commissioned murals on public buildings from Rivera and others.
Man at the Crossroads (1933) at Rockefeller Center was covered and then destroyed in early 1934 after Rivera refused to remove Lenin's portrait.
